edge_transition_width — 2D edges op

• Data kinds: image → image

• Call: fullseye.apply(img, "edge_transition_width", a=0.5, b=0.5) (the 2-D model is one image plus two scalar knobs a,b∈[0,1])

*The 4th column is a colour (H,W,3) input. This op handles colour without crossing channels (it does not convolve the colour channel as a third spatial axis).*

Usage

Measures the edge transition width (= the spread of the effective PSF at that location) in pixels.

a sweeps the side length of the measurement window over 3,5,7,9 (_k(a)). b selects the estimator for amplitude and

gradient: b <= 0.5 uses the in-window max − min (simple and sharp but weak against outliers), b > 0.5 uses quantiles, and the higher b, the more the quantiles move from 90/10 towards 60/40, becoming duller to noise (and steps get rounded correspondingly = it is a trade-off).

Width ≒ local amplitude ÷ local maximum gradient. If a step rises within 1 pixel the width is around 1; if it is blurred and rises over 5 pixels, around 5. It is the counterpart of simulate_defocus, which creates blur; this op is the side that measures it. Usable for focus judgement, amount of motion blur, resolution limit and judging whether text is large enough to read.

If the window is narrower than the transition, the width is underestimated (because the full amplitude does not fit in the window). The practical rule: if the output exceeds 0.7, raise a and measure again.

Normalisation is not per image (it only divides by the constant window side), so values can be compared across images. An output of 1.0 means "the transition width equals the window = it may be wider than the window and was not fully measured", and is the signal to raise a and measure again. Flat areas and places without edges give 0.

★Returns all 0 on an empty frame ("no edge"). If the floor is set only as a quantity relative to the image's own amplitude, then on a uniform image even the reference turns into rounding dust and the ratio of dust to dust turns into structure ——

measured: an image that was just a flat 0.5 with 1e-12 noise added returned a width of 3.49 (= half the window). We state flatly that an image whose amplitude itself does not reach the absolute floor 1e-6 has no edge. Border handling is the scipy.ndimage default reflect. There is no internal step that drops to 8 bit.
